title: DRV Book I  -  The Lock  -  REWRITE v2

canonical_node.axiom: The ground of mathematical and moral truth is the Logos, functionally identical to God-as-Axiom, the first primitive axiom of the Formal Theory v1.0.
definitions: Truth: below-floor presupposition exhibiting seven properties: existence, temporal independence, necessity, universality, eternality, immateriality, coherence.
Logos: the name for the ground of mathematical and moral truth, chosen for its semantic range (rational structure, ordering principle, meaningful speech, account).

God-as-Axiom: the terminal ground required by the von Neumann measurement chain, the regress argument, and the open-system requirement; named 'God' in classical theism, 'Logos' in the Johannine prologue, 'uncaused cause' in scholastic philosophy.
Central Claim: the thesis that mathematical and moral truth share a single ground; operationalized by the Master Equation.
Source-Property Transmission Lemma: a single inference that transfers properties from the source to what it grounds.
derivation: Layer 0: Seven properties of mathematical truth are observed as below-floor presuppositions (P0.1 - P0.7).
Layer 1: Gdel-Chaitin theorem (external) establishes that the ground of mathematical truth is external to mathematics.
Layer 2: From the theorem, the ground cannot be nothing, cannot be chaos, cannot be deceptive (Inferences 2.1 - 2.3).
Layer 3: Source-Property Transmission Lemma transfers the seven properties plus veracity to the ground.
Layer 4: Definitions and postulates: truth is valuable, deception is wrong.
Layer 5: Central Claim: the source of mathematical truth and the source of moral truth are one.
Layer 6: The ground is named the Logos (Definition 6.1) and identified as Axiom 1 (God-as-Axiom).
canonical_node.action: The framework should present the argument from properties of truth to the Logos as a layered derivation, with Layer 0 as below-floor presuppositions, Layer 1 as an external theorem, Layers 2 - 3 as inferences, Layer 4 as definitions/postulates, Layer 5 as the defended thesis, and Layer 6 as the naming and identification with the primitive axiom.
boundary: Does not assert the seven properties as axioms; they are below-floor presuppositions.
Does not claim the Gdel-Chaitin theorem as an axiom of the framework; it is an inherited result.
Does not treat the Central Claim as an axiom; it is the thesis to be defended.
Does not push beyond the Feb 14 floor into divine mechanics (how God operates internally, why God chose this design, what exists before/outside the system).
Does not exercise Axiom 2 (Trinity Isomorphism) in this series; it is acknowledged but not load-bearing here.
test: Check that each layer's epistemic status is correctly labeled (below-floor, external theorem, inference, definition/postulate, central claim, naming definition, primitive axiom).
Verify that the Source-Property Transmission Lemma is applied correctly to transfer properties.
Confirm that the Central Claim is presented as the thesis, not as an assumed axiom.
Ensure that the Feb 14 floor is explicitly stated as the intentional formal boundary.

dg1_dependencies: Empirical evidence from I (pre-linguistic numeracy and pre-socialized moral evaluation data)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a reclassified, layered argument from properties of truth to the Logos, distinguishing epistemic statuses (below-floor, theorem, inference, definition, central claim, axiom) and explicitly identifying the Feb 14 floor with three primitive axioms.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the content of the original twenty axioms while reclassifying them; maintains the conclusion that the ground is the Logos, functionally identical to God-as-Axiom.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, the framework loses its explicit reclassification of the axiom chain, reverting to a flat-axiom structure that misrepresents the May 10 canon; the argument's epistemic load-bearing distinctions would be lost.
dg5_translation_registers: Philosophical: identity of indiscernibles, principle of sufficient reason
Formal: Formal Theory v1.0, primitive axioms

overstatement_risks: Treating below-floor properties as axioms despite reclassification
Treating the Central Claim as proven rather than defended
Overstating the force of the identity of indiscernibles argument
Conflating the Gdel-Chaitin theorem with a proof of the Logos' existence
kill_conditions: If the Gdel-Chaitin theorem is misapplied or misinterpreted
If the Source-Property Transmission Lemma is invalid
If the Central Claim is shown to be false or unsupported
If the Feb 14 floor is violated by asserting divine mechanics
risk.lean_target: The argument is a structured theological derivation, not a formal proof; it should be treated as a narrative anchor with epistemic distinctions.

plain_summary: This document rewrites Section III of DRV Book I, reclassifying the original twenty axioms into a layered argument: seven below-floor properties of truth, an external Gdel-Chaitin theorem, derived inferences, a transmission lemma, definitions and postulates, a central claim, and finally the identification of the Logos with God-as-Axiom. It explicitly sets the Feb 14 floor as the boundary of formal reach. The document is a coherent reclassification but does not establish the truth of its central claim; it is a theological argument, not a formal proof.
